commits.message: docs(style): params is the raw field, id= included
fix(osc8): review — text.ts names the wire enforcer; pin a ';' in the URI

fix(osc8): one terminator set, UTF-8 id hash, typed read-back

Review fixes for the OSC 8 link-id change.

- osc8.ts absorbs sanitize.ts: the sanitizer, the producer and the
  reader now read one TERMINATORS constant. The reader previously
  stopped only at ESC \ and BEL while the sanitizer also treated the
  8-bit ST (0x9C) as a terminator; a 0x9C-terminated link was counted
  as visible width by any measure built on OSC8.source.
- linkId hashes the URL's UTF-8 bytes, so the id is standard FNV-1a
  that another runtime can reproduce (it hashed UTF-16 code units).
- osc8Sequences(text) is the typed read-back ({index, length, params,
  uri}); OSC8 stays exported for composing into a larger pattern.
  Tests and the coverage demo read through it instead of re-spelling
  the grammar or remapping positional groups.
- Docs state that same-URL spans hover as one link even when not
  adjacent (deliberate: same URL, same click), pinned by a test.
- CLAUDE.md tier map: osc8 replaces sanitize at tier 0.

feat(osc8): every link carries an id derived from its URL, so a split link hovers as one

A terminal treats cells as one hyperlink when they share the URI and the id.
With empty params, each OSC 8 open was its own link, and the coalescer can only
share one pair across a run of identical SGR — so a link whose text changes
style mid-span (a bold glyph beside plain text) highlighted in pieces on hover.

The id is FNV-1a of the sanitized URI: the byte stream stays a pure function of
(style, text, colorSystem), which is why the id was dropped in the first place.
Terminals key on the (id, URI) pair, so a hash collision merges nothing.

The OSC 8 open/close was spelled by hand at both producers (segmentsToString,
Style.render); both now call osc8Open / OSC8_CLOSE in core/osc8.ts. OSC8, the
read-back pattern, is exported for consumers that parse rendered bytes.

feat(export)!: theme-aware, attribute-complete HTML export (rich-export-9a1.2) (#151) * feat(export)!: theme-aware, attribute-complete HTML export (rich-export-9a1.2) Console.exportHtml({ theme?, clear? }) now draws exportLines' resolved picture through a new core module, export-html (encodeHtml). The page's background and default text colour come from the theme via a new exportCanvas in export-lines, the same ground resolveLook flattens runs over. Every ExportLook field is written: reverse and dim arrive as resolved colours (no opacity), double underline, strike, overline, blink via keyframes, frame and encircle, and allowed links as elements. Refused links export as styled text. pre no longer re-wraps recorded rows. saveHtml and saveText take the full option type of the export they write. BREAKING CHANGE: Style.getHtmlStyle is removed with no replacement; export through Console.exportHtml. The exported HTML markup changes shape. * fix(export): a double underline no longer doubles strike and overline CSS gives an element one text-decoration-style, so underline2 sharing a span with strike drew a double strike-through the terminal never showed. The double underline now sits on an outer span carrying the paint (so no inner background covers it) and the blink (so it blinks with the glyph); strike and overline stay single on the inner span. Checked in headless Chromium over a painted background. * fix(export): a trailing blank row is drawn in the HTML export A newline straight before ends a line without drawing another, so a recording ending in a blank row lost it. Every row now ends with its own newline, matching the newline the page writes after 
 for the parser to
drop. Checked in headless Chromium: the pre's height in lines equals
exportLines' row count for blank rows first, last, both and in between.
